page: The Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-640s-amd is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The hardware profile includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 640 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing the server in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth consistently rank in the average tier. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and database operations on PassMark fall into the weak tier. Large language model inference speeds are also limited, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model registering in the bottom 10% tier, while text generation for the same model remains in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 alongside substantial local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extreme multi-threaded compute. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. Suitable workloads include caching layers, memory-intensive web applications, moderate database operations, and general-purpose tasks requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute resources.
